findings.detail: This PR adds a local control surface that can close serving admission, cancel in-flight inference after 120s, and unload every model. Callers are code-signature-authenticated sockets (AddonPeerPolicy.authenticate) and the operator mailbox (handleAddonControl). No TB/T entry covers this boundary: socket location and permissions, per-connection versus per-request authentication, lease bounds, or the rule that an expired lease is kept while the machine lock is held (ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift:322-334, 142-146). The lock appears to be observed through a plain file, so any same-UID process that takes it could keep the provider held indefinitely. The same-UID user is already the operator (ADV-001), so this is an availability and documentation gap rather than a confidentiality regression. Fix: add a TB entry and threat for the add-on hold, recording the peer policy, lease clamps, machine-lock semantics and fail-open on an unreadable hold record (ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift:366-368).
findings.title: New add-on local IPC/mailbox control channel is not covered by the threat model

findings.detail: docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md documents a new local AF_UNIX `hold.v1` control surface (~/.darkbloom/runtime/addon.sock). Over it, a code-signed add-on can make the provider drain or hold serving capacity, and an expired lease is kept while the add-on holds ownership.lock. The doc points readers to threat-model `TB-012` (line 96), but the base canonical model defines boundaries only through TB-011. No asset, threat or mitigation covers this boundary. Nothing in the model covers the same-user peer-token and code-requirement check, the DEBUG-only `DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY` acceptance, the `DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET` path override, or the indefinite availability hold through ownership.lock. The new `darkbloom addon` lifecycle-mailbox commands in cli-reference.md are also unmodeled. Trigger: a reviewer relies on TB-012 to evaluate this surface, but no TB-012 exists. Impact: provider availability and drain controls stay unreviewed against TB-003 and TB-002. The model also does not record that busy fields reported to the coordinator are self-reported. Fix: add TB-012 and its threats to docs/threat-model.yaml. The new entries should record that the socket is not a boundary against the same user. They should state whether release builds honor DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET. They should also bound how long a hold can persist.
